chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Amr, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ya'fur, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If you doubt about something from the wudu (ablution) after you have entered into something else, then your doubt is nothing. Doubt only counts when you are still in a thing and have not yet passed beyond it.

key_terms.الشَّكُّ: doubt or uncertainty regarding whether an act was performed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.بِشَيْءٍ: of any consequence or legal effect
key_terms.دَخَلْتَ: you entered into or proceeded to another act or stage
key_terms.غَيْرِهِ: something other than it, meaning a subsequent act or step
key_terms.لَمْ تَجُزْهُ: you have not yet passed beyond it

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I doubt a part of my wudu (ablution) after moving on to the next step?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding doubt in wudu (ablution). If a person doubts a part of the wudu (ablution) after having moved on from it, the doubt is disregarded; relevant doubt is only that which occurs before one has passed beyond the act in question.
